The Northwest region was fit by weighted least squares, not GLS (ver. 1.1 changed it; Table 1-4 footnote 3, Table 1-5 footnote 2): its model error variance is printed 0.000 for Q4 through Q0.2 and is stored as 0.0, so its site-specific prediction variance is x'Ux alone; its covariance entries are printed to fewer digits than the GLS regions'. Report inconsistency (not in this file): the Case 3 example (p. 24) evaluates the East-Central Plains Q2 equation with a = 433, but Table 1-4 and NSS give 497; Table 1-4 is used. CHANNEL-WIDTH METHODS (regions '<region>-AC', '-BF', '-RS'). Source: Chase, Sando, Armstrong and McCarthy, 2021, SIR 2020-5142 ver. 1.1 (September 2021; the version history revises five exponents in Tables 2 and 4, all as stored). For each of the 8 hydrologic regions and 10 AEPs, one equation per method: AC active-channel width (Table 2, NSS code WACTCH), BF bankfull width (Table 3, WBANKFULL) and RS channel width measured from aerial photographs (Table 4, CHANWD_RS), all in feet, of the form Q = K W^b (eq. 4), stored as intercept = log10(K) and the width log10. Width limits are Table 1's (NSS's are identical). The schema has no method tag and StateLibrary.equation looks up by region code alone, so each method gets its own region code, the hydrologic-region code plus '-AC', '-BF' or '-RS' (NSS GC1829-GC1852, regression regions 858-881, citation 163; each region_name names its NSS code); the basin-characteristics codes are unchanged. Error statistics: the channel-width regressions add a measurement error variance (MEV) for the measured width, and the report's site SEP is sqrt(sigma_delta^2 + MEV + x'Ux) (pp. 41-44), so model_error_variance stores sigma_delta^2 + MEV and evaluate()'s site-specific interval is the report's. MVP excludes MEV (on all 240 rows the SEP converted to log units squared equals MVP + MEV to the printed rounding, within 0.0016), so avp stores MVP + MEV; sep_log is the SEP converted as sqrt(ln(1 + (SEP/100)^2)) / ln(10). n_sites is each table's n (smaller for Q66.7 in several regions). The Northwest region is WLS: its sigma_delta^2 is printed 0.000 at several AEPs, so there model_error_variance is MEV alone. Covariance [X^T Lambda^-1 X]^-1 from Tables 7 (AC), 8 (BF) and 9 (RS), intercept then log10(width), as printed; both triangles are printed and every matrix is symmetric. Tables 1-4, 6 and 7-9 were double-entered (hand transcription from rendered pages vs. a regex parse of pdftotext -table output): 3,648 cells, 0 disagreements; all 240 NSS equation strings (citation 163) carry the same K and b. Table 6's cross-correlations between methods' residuals are stored under the top-level key 'cross_correlations' (outside the equation schema, which the library ignores) and used by flowfreq.regression.montana.estimate_weighted, which combines two or three methods at a site by the report's eqs. 5-12 (Parrett and Johnson, 2004); evaluate_weighted cannot, as its weights are fixed fractions. The report's worked examples reproduce (examples 1-3: 432 cfs SEPz 0.217; 415 and 257 cfs, area-weighted 358; 44.7 cfs SEPz 0.543) to the report's own intermediate rounding. Report inconsistencies (not in this file): example 3 calls Q66.7 the '1.5-percent AEP' flood; example 1 prints weights 0.623, 0.332, 0.045 computed from A, B and C rounded to 3 decimals (the system is ill-conditioned; unrounded weights are 0.624, 0.356, 0.019 with the same Z and SEPz); example 1's basin-characteristics estimate is 551 from rounded factors (558 unrounded). NSS discrepancy: its ASEp for NWF active-channel Q10 is 65.5, Table 2 prints 65.6.

cross_correlations.description: Cross-correlation coefficients between regression residuals of pairs of estimation methods, by hydrologic region and AEP. BC is the basin-characteristics method (this file's regions W, NW, ..., SW; SIR 2015-5019-F); AC, BF and RS are the channel-width methods (regions '<region>-AC', '-BF', '-RS'). Used by flowfreq.regression.montana to weight combined estimates (report eqs. 5-12). Not part of the equation schema; flowfreq.regression.library ignores this key.
